blocks.text: Origin / creation. Archive stewards, provenance specialists, canonical curators, and heritage authorities gained social rank as preservation demands intensified.
Identity / human status. Artificial professional and political classes. They were internally divided; many archivists opposed heritage freezing.
Importance. They saved immense quantities of language, art, law, ecology, and memory from immediate loss.

Decline or degradation. Control over canonical versions centralized historical authority. Heritage Freezing converted living traditions into performances, while archive scale overwhelmed witness and maintenance.

Final status / surviving function. Fragmented during preservation failure. Material entered compressed or sleeping archives. Their mixed legacy is survival of knowledge alongside loss of living context.
